Thanks Lauren — adding some technical clarity from NetOps perspective. I’ve also pasted a short checklist we typically use for Private VPC onboarding below.

PrivateLink vs VPC Peering
- PrivateLink: easier for cross-account AWS customers, simplified IAM surface (we present an endpoint in FinPay account). Slightly higher per-request latency (~1–3 ms) but better isolation.
- VPC Peering: direct L3 connectivity, lower latency, but requires route table + potential IP overlap handling on FinPay side. Not ideal if you want strong tenant isolation.

Egress and allowlist guidance
- For staging: Redwood can provide a stable IPv4 set (3 addresses) from our NAT pool used for staging. For production, we recommend assigning a customer-dedicated NAT pool (static IPs) — this is available on Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Common ports to allow: 443 (TLS), 80 (health check redirect), 12345 (internal metrics webhook — optional). We’ll provide a full FQDN list (metrics.redwood-inference.com, cb-svc.redwood-inference.com) in the runbook.
- mTLS: supported. If FinPay elects to manage certs, we’ll publish the CSR process; otherwise Redwood can terminate TLS and enforce mutual auth to customer backends if required.

Onboarding checklist (short)
1) Confirm CIDRs and firewall owner.
2) Choose endpoint type (PrivateLink or Peering).
3) Allowlist staging egress IPs.
4) Provision staging tenant and smoke tests.
5) Run integration tests and security signoffs.
6) Production NAT assignment and cutover date.

Links: https://docs.redwood.com/privatenet/allowlist-playbook (internal doc)

Priyom — can you prepare the staging IP set and a minimal FQDN list? I can share those by EOD June 11 if that timeline works.
